Without the hyphen, CONCAT('A001', CAST(12 AS STRING)) produces 'A00112', and CONCAT('A0011', CAST(2 AS STRING)) also produces 'A00112'. Two different subscriptions, one primary key.'

contract-driven-data-transformation: 'field: campaign_id mode: NULLABLE nulls: 100% -> EXPECTED (mode allows NULL) / field: current_state mode: REQUIRED nulls: 100% -> INVESTIGATE / raw check: $.current_state exists in source JSON? YES -> EXTRACTION BUG ... NO -> SOURCE CHANGED'

contract-driven-data-transformation: 'For three source tables, just hand-write the SQL and move on with your life. The overhead of maintaining contracts and a generator isn't justified when you can see the entire staging layer on a single screen. For thirty tables, the math flips.'
contract-driven-data-transformation: 'The mess isn't caused by humans or AI - it's caused by the absence of a shared specification.'

the-rise-of-model-driven-data-engineer: 'DAS represents source systems without interpretation through two stages: landing zone and staging. Landing receives raw data exactly as produced - often JSON strings with no schema enforcement. Staging unpacks to tabular format while remaining faithful to source structure.'

the-rise-of-model-driven-data-engineer: 'Ingestion is forgiving (accept all data as JSON); unpacking is strict (contract-driven). Data is never lost when schemas change. If sources send incorrect data then corrections, "latest" views automatically reflect the corrected state.'
the-rise-of-model-driven-data-engineer: 'Contracts are truth; SQL is artifact.'

the-rise-of-model-driven-data-engineer (the ACID TEST): 'is your contract documentation that someone manually keeps in sync with custom SQL, or does it directly generate unpacking logic? The first improves documentation. The second unifies documentation and implementation.'

design-of-analytical-systems: 'The philosophy is forgiving ingestion - accept all data as it arrives - combined with strict unpacking, where structure and quality are enforced through data contracts at the staging boundary.' and 'This layer often manifests as two physical layers: a raw landing zone and a staging area.'
design-of-analytical-systems: 'DAS also provides reloadability - if transformation logic in DAB changes, we can reprocess from DAS without going back to source systems.'

the-work-before-the-answer (Calle Wilund): 'We ingest the data raw from source with everything in a big JSON blob. Then we have a data contract for each source, owned by the data producing product team, that lists how this raw data should be unpacked into a structured format. The actual SQL ... is then auto-generated by scripts that read each contract.'

the-work-before-the-answer: 'In the old platform, we ingested data into structured tables (i.e. we had committed to a schema during ingestion), which always created issues when source schema changed.' and 'every staging table will work exactly the same across all sources.'

the-work-before-the-answer: 'a silent identifier collision ... Two records that should have been distinct were being merged into one because of how I'd composed the identifier. The bug had been in the DAS for weeks, invisible because nothing downstream was looking at it.'

ai-assisted-data-engineering: 'YAML data contracts define the rules. The agent works within them. The constraints are features: you can't accidentally inject business logic into pure staging.' and 'Each contract specifies a single source-to-staging transformation: which raw table to read, what fields to extract, how to type-cast them, what expected values look like.'
blog-synthesis dasConstraints: 'The latest view must be a late-arriving-correction-tolerant projection over historized data ... Not a snapshot, not first-write-wins.'

blog-synthesis dasConstraints: 'DAS output must be typed AND documented at column level; column descriptions must actually be populated in the warehouse because every agent reads INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMN_FIELD_PATHS before writing SQL.'

blog-synthesis contradictions: 'DAS CAPTURE AND PERSIST ONLY vs CONTRACT-DRIVEN STAGING ... Either the blueprint's DAS is only the landing zone (and staging is unlabelled), or the staging step violates a stated absolute.'

blog-synthesis mustBeInvented: the contract example 'is Kafka-specific, has a primary key with no matching column, and carries no ownership field despite work-before-the-answer making ownership the whole point.'

spike 1 finding 2 (observed): '@dlt.resource(columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}}) yielding a real dict under payload keeps the whole record in ONE column of dlt type json. No columns are inferred from inside it.'

spike 1 finding 14 (observed): 'a plain read_parquet glob over an append-only lake SILENTLY DROPS columns added in later loads - no error, just missing data. union_by_name => true fixes it.' Evidence shows _new_prov_col absent with no error, present with union_by_name.

spike 1 finding 15 (observed): 'DuckDB JSON operators work directly on the VARCHAR payload column with an implicit cast - no explicit ::JSON needed. ->> yields VARCHAR (then CAST), -> yields JSON, plus json_keys / json_array_length / json_extract.' json_keys returned the 14 Northwind Order properties.

spike 1 finding 16 (observed): 'freight is DOUBLE when dlt infers it (approach C), but DECIMAL(18,4) when cast explicitly out of the JSON column. This is a concrete argument for the two-layer design.'

spike 1 finding 13 (observed): "dataset_name='das__raw' is silently normalised to 'das_raw'. Passing enable_dataset_name_normalization=False on the destination preserves the literal 'das__raw' folder."

spike 1 finding 17 (observed): hive-style date partitioning works via the filesystem layout parameter, but 'the placeholder names are {YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}, not {year}/{month}/{day}' - {year} raises InvalidFilesystemLayout.
spike 1 finding 11 (observed): '_dlt_id is a per-row-instance surrogate, NOT a stable record identity. The same source record (OrderId 10248) got a different _dlt_id in each load.'

spike 1 finding 8 and 4 (observed): the landed payload reads back as VARCHAR, and dlt's json data_type is byte-identical to text in parquet ('BYTE_ARRAY / UTF8 / StringType()'), so the strict layer must always cast.

spike 1 gotcha (observed): 'Two identical runs produce 240 rows for 120 distinct orders. Append-only is correct for DAS but das__staged as written duplicates rows - a dedup/latest-version step (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY das_extracted_at DESC)) is needed before DAB consumes it.'

spike 1 gotcha (observed): 'Relative paths inside a DuckDB view's read_parquet() resolve against the DuckDB process's cwd at QUERY time, not at CREATE VIEW time... Use absolute paths, or a DuckDB variable/macro for the lake root.'

task brief, reporting spike 1: 'hive partition columns come back VARCHAR without hive_types' - this specific observation is stated in the brief rather than in the spike-findings JSON I read, and I am attributing it as the brief states it.

spike 2 finding 8 (observed): 'FULL_LOG is IDEMPOTENT. Re-running execute ... against a view holding TWO rows for the same primary key ... leave the _desc base table byte-stable' (25 rows across runs 7 and 8).

spike 2 finding 9 (observed): 'FULL IS NOT IDEMPOTENT against a multi-row-per-primary-key source view. It inserts exactly ONE duplicate _desc row per execute ... Growth is unbounded and the presentation views MASK it completely' (22 -> 23 -> 24 -> 25).

spike 2 finding 6 (observed): 'With entity_effective_timestamp_expression: das_load_ts, eff_tmstp in view_<entity>_hist IS the DAS load timestamp verbatim' - both versions retained in hist, only the new one in the current view.
spike 2 finding 7 (observed): unchanged attribute values are not re-versioned ('customer_name and customer_id got none'), so DAS does not need a record hash for DAB to avoid spurious versions.

spike 2 finding 2 (observed): 'Reading a VIEW as a mapping source is a non-issue' - daana consumed das__staged views 'with no complaint and no special configuration', with primary_keys given as a list.

spike 2 finding 11 (observed): any other open connection to the .duckdb file - even read-only - makes daana-cli execute fail with the misleading error 'daana framework is not installed on the remote database'.
daana-cli-0-7-0-release: 'FULL_LOG continues to soft-delete rows for source-row disappearance.'
spike 4 finding 6 (observed): 'AL09 is the single most dangerous rule for this build ... It fired twice on o.order_id AS order_id' - which conventions §3 already excludes for exactly this reason.

spike 4 findings 2 and 3 (observed): the duckdb dialect is required, not merely nicer - postgres 'fails to parse the QUALIFY clause entirely' - and on well-formatted generated SQL with cast(x AS DECIMAL(28,8)) and QUALIFY row_number() OVER (...), only RF06 fires.

spike 4 finding 12 (observed): yamllint on a data-contract YAML fires document-start (missing ---) and line-length; short flow mappings like {source_path: OrderId, target_name: order_id, type: INTEGER} are accepted by the default braces rule.
notSettled: Whether sqlfluff's duckdb dialect parses the JSON arrow operators (`->>`, `->`), `try_cast(...)`, and the `hive_types => {'extracted_on': DATE}` struct-literal named argument. Spike 4 exercised cast(), QUALIFY and quoted reserved words only. If any of these fail to parse, the gate blocks the whole layer and the fallback is the byte-equivalent function form (json_extract_string / json_extract) — decide this before writing the generator, not after.

Whether sqlfluff's CV11 (convention.casting_style, set to prefer `cast`) accepts `try_cast` at all. It is neither `cast`, nor `::`, nor `convert`, and spike 4 only observed CV11 firing on `::`. If CV11 rejects try_cast, either the rule is configured differently or the whole cast/try_cast decision is forced.

Whether DuckDB's COMMENT ON COLUMN works against a VIEW's columns and survives CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW. No spike touched it. The synthesis requires column descriptions to be populated in the warehouse because agents read the catalog before writing SQL; if comments do not survive, the fallback (the contract file as the only doc surface, printed by the CLI) is weaker and should be argued separately.

The timezone of dlt's {YYYY}-{MM}-{DD} layout placeholder versus to_timestamp's UTC. Spike 1 verified the placeholder names, not the midnight boundary. A load just either side of midnight UTC could land in a partition that disagrees with its own extracted_at. The generated check catches it after the fact; nothing prevents it.

Whether enable_dataset_name_normalization=False also stops TABLE-name normalisation. Spike 1 lists this as untested and it bites the moment a contract stem must come from an entity set like OrderDetails, which is exactly the next contract this system will need.

Whether `cast` (raises loudly, breaks readability, fires non-deterministically under projection pushdown) or `try_cast` (quiet, NULL, caught only by a check) is right for a REQUIRED column. This is a judgement about which failure the team prefers, not a fact either source settles; the blog uses SAFE_CAST uniformly and the blueprint's S3 argues the other way.

The word for the deduplicated projection. The blog says `latest`; this repository already spells the same idea `_is_current` in DAR (conventions §1.3). I have chosen `current` in both the contract and the object name so one idea has one word, but this is a coin flip and the only thing that matters is that the loser is never used again.

Whether the type vocabulary needs a format template. Every Northwind Edm.Date and Edm.Decimal cast cleanly in spike 1, so DATE/TIMESTAMP need no parse string today. The first source that sends a non-ISO date has no way to say so, and the choice is between a strptime template on the column and a new vocabulary entry per format — the blog's dictionary approach implies the latter.

Delete detection. DAS as designed cannot express 'this key was absent from load N', and neither the log nor the current view triggers daana's FULL_LOG soft-delete. Answering it needs a third projection over the most recent load only. Nobody has designed it and slice 1 does not need it, but the gap should be recorded before someone assumes soft-delete works.

Whether a record hash belongs in DAS. Spike 1 shows _dlt_id is not stable across loads, so content identity would have to be our own column; spike 2 shows daana already suppresses unchanged attributes, so DAB does not need it. That leaves 'did this load change anything at all?' as a full comparison rather than a hash compare — cheap now, expensive at volume.

Small-file and full-scan behaviour. Spike 1 measured 120 rows and explicitly did not measure DuckDB scanning hundreds of per-load parquet files, nor daana's FULL_LOG re-reading the whole log every execute. There is no compaction design and S2 makes the obvious one (rewriting files) illegal.

Contract granularity. The corpus contradicts itself — 'a data contract for each source' versus 'Each contract specifies a single source-to-staging transformation'. I have chosen one file per landed table because conventions §1.1 ties the file stem to the table name, but the ownership model in the blog is per-source and the two do not line up when one source has thirty entity sets.

How a source property whose name is a SQL reserved word, or contains a dot, or differs from another only by case, is represented. `source_path` has no quoting or escaping rule, and `target_name` is required to be the mechanical snake_case of it. DAR's precedent is to quote (dar__uss."order"), but nothing decides it for DAS.

Whether the CI protocol is a decision of this ADR or of the CI ADR. The safety of the two-object design depends entirely on CI replaying the fixture twice; with one replay the log and the current view are identical and none of this is tested. That protocol has to be owned somewhere explicitly.
data.recommendation: das__staged is the change log (one row per source record per load), and the same contract also generates a deduplicated das__staged.<table>__current beside it
data.title: A DAS data contract is one YAML artefact that is documentation, schema and transformation at once, and it generates a forgiving das__raw view over the landed parquet plus a strict das__staged change log and a das__staged.<table>__current projection beside it
